I’m planning a cozy Christmas day at home with my toddler and want ideas for both of us that I can actually look at on screen afterward. Once you’ve got the toddler plan sorted, switch over to Scratch Magazine and look for Grinch Christmas nail inspiration, then find one Grinch tutorial page I could realistically follow and leave that tutorial page open so I can check the design details myself. From there, go to Amazon and find at least three Grinch-themed nail art ideas or products that use different materials, like stickers or decals, gel polish, brushes, glitter, rhinestones, stamping plates, or similar, and make sure they actually fit the style or techniques shown on the Scratch tutorial. Please open the most promising Amazon product pages in their own tabs so I can compare them visually, and then give me a clear summary with the toddler activity options, the Scratch tutorial, and the three nail product ideas with links plus a quick note on how each one matches the Grinch look.

Christmas character nail art: how to paint the Grinch

Seasonal & Occasions, Step by Step

You’re a mean one, Mr Grinch! UK freehand nail artist, Gemma Dawson
(opens in new tab)
, has created this Grinch nail design, perfect for the festive season.

Email(Required)

SIGN UP NOW
Step 1
Paint a nail tip a light green gel polish colour, cure, then apply a non-wipe top coat and cure.
Step 2
Using a dark green or black gel paint, add a small mushroom shape in the centre of the tip and paint a vertical line down from it.
Step 3
Paint a lopsided semicircle at the bottom of the vertical line.
Step 4
Paint a line across that, to make the Grinch's pouting lip. Cure.
Step 5
Directly above each side of the nose, paint two dark green curved lines and cure.
Step 6
Add two black lines that curve in the opposite direction and meet in the middle. These will become the eyebrows.
Step 7
Bring the black lines under and join them up to make two eye shapes. Cure.
Step 8
Leave a gap before painting four dark green semicircles above the brows.
Step 9
Use where the circles end as a guide to join up the outline of the Grinch's head shape, and bring his chin to a point in the dark green hue.
Step 10
Whilst the gel is still wet, use a thicker brush to drag out the edges. This will create the appearance of fur. Cure.
Step 11
Paint the Grinch's eyes with a white gel paint and his nose dark green. Also paint a line of dark green under his lip. Cure.
Step 12
Paint the lip pink and cure.
Step 13
Start filling in the eyebrows with black gel and the head area with dark green. Use the thicker brush to drag the product to give a furry finish. Cure.
Step 14
Using the same dragging technique, paint the rest of the Grinch's face with a green gel that is a few shades lighter, apart from around his nose. Cure.
Step 15
Add more dark green to the face, layering and dragging to make the Grinch look furry. Cure. Paint some green mixed with top coat on the underside of the eyes, to create a shadow. Cure.
Step 16
Add some finer lines of dark green or black to outline the fur. Also add some black to the nostrils and cure. Paint the Grinch's irises using a bright midtone green. Cure.
Step 17
Outline the eyes in black and add pupils. Then, using a fine liner brush, add thin black lines to the brows to give definition and make them look bushier. Cure. Blacken around the Grinch's eyes and brows, and add any additional fur. Cure.
Step 18
Using a fine liner brush, paint a few thin lines of pale green gel through the brows and on top of the nose to act as a highlight. Cure.
Step 19
Apply top coat and cure to finish.

   - **URL:** https://www.hobbycraft.co.uk/ideas/how-to-make-paper-plate-angels.html
   - **Materials Needed:** White paper plates (10-pack), metallic marker pens (recommended by Hobbycraft over messy glitter glue), white pipe cleaners (for halos), yarn scraps (for hair), black marker pen (for drawing eyes and smile), child-safe scissors, and a glue stick.
   - **Why It’s Toddler-Friendly & Low-Mess:** There is zero loose glitter or runny paint. The toddler can color the paper plate wings and dress with washable metallic markers, glue soft yarn hair onto the angel head, and bend the soft pipe cleaner into a halo with your help.

   - **Tab:** Tab 103795304
   - **Page Title:** How to Make Fillable Baubles | Hobbycraft

   - **Why It’s Toddler-Friendly & Low-Mess:** Toddlers love "posting" and dropping objects into containers. Source page opened in **Tab 103795306** (*15 Easy Christmas Activities for Toddlers (1-Minute Setup!)* at https://toddlerinaction.com/easy-christmas-activities-at-home-your-toddler-will-love/).

   - **Concept:** A completely mess-free sensory experience. A heavy-duty zip-top freezer bag is filled with water or clear hair gel, along with green pom-poms, glitter sequins, and cut-out foam trees. The bag is securely sealed with duct tape and taped flat to a low window or high-chair tray.
   - **Why It’s Different:** It provides rich tactile, squishing, and pushing sensory play without any craft debris, glue, or stains.

Christmas character nail art: how to paint the Grinch

Seasonal & Occasions, Step by Step

You’re a mean one, Mr Grinch! UK freehand nail artist, Gemma Dawson
(opens in new tab)
, has created this Grinch nail design, perfect for the festive season.

Are you enjoying this content?

Join our community to receive more like this

Email(Required)
Click here
(opens in new tab)
 to see how we use your personal data
SIGN UP NOW
Step 1
Paint a nail tip a light green gel polish colour, cure, then apply a non-wipe top coat and cure.
Step 2
Using a dark green or black gel paint, add a small mushroom shape in the centre of the tip and paint a vertical line down from it.
Step 3
Paint a lopsided semicircle at the bottom of the vertical line.
Step 4
Paint a line across that, to make the Grinch's pouting lip. Cure.
Step 5
Directly above each side of the nose, paint two dark green curved lines and cure.
Step 6
Add two black lines that curve in the opposite direction and meet in the middle. These will become the eyebrows.
Step 7
Bring the black lines under and join them up to make two eye shapes. Cure.
Step 8
Leave a gap before painting four dark green semicircles above the brows.
Step 9
Use where the circles end as a guide to join up the outline of the Grinch's head shape, and bring his chin to a point in the dark green hue.
Step 10
Whilst the gel is still wet, use a thicker brush to drag out the edges. This will create the appearance of fur. Cure.
Step 11
Paint the Grinch's eyes with a white gel paint and his nose dark green. Also paint a line of dark green under his lip. Cure.
Step 12
Paint the lip pink and cure.
Step 13
Start filling in the eyebrows with black gel and the head area with dark green. Use the thicker brush to drag the product to give a furry finish. Cure.
Step 14
Using the same dragging technique, paint the rest of the Grinch's face with a green gel that is a few shades lighter, apart from around his nose. Cure.
Step 15
Add more dark green to the face, layering and dragging to make the Grinch look furry. Cure. Paint some green mixed with top coat on the underside of the eyes, to create a shadow. Cure.
Step 16
Add some finer lines of dark green or black to outline the fur. Also add some black to the nostrils and cure. Paint the Grinch's irises using a bright midtone green. Cure.
Step 17
Outline the eyes in black and add pupils. Then, using a fine liner brush, add thin black lines to the brows to give definition and make them look bushier. Cure. Blacken around the Grinch's eyes and brows, and add any additional fur. Cure.
Step 18
Using a fine liner brush, paint a few thin lines of pale green gel through the brows and on top of the nose to act as a highlight. Cure.
Step 19
Apply top coat and cure to finish.

   - **Why It’s Different:** It provides rich tactile, squishing, and pushing sensory play without any craft debris, glue, or stains.

2. **Jingle Bell Scooping, Pouring & Auditory Sort**
   - **Concept:** Place a variety of colorful jingle bells in a shallow plastic tub alongside child-sized measuring cups, silicone muffin cups, and large toddler spoons or scoops. 
   - **Why It’s Different:** Focuses on auditory feedback and fine-motor coordination. As toddlers scoop, transfer, and drop bells between containers, they are rewarded with cheerful holiday chime sounds.

3. **Fine-Motor "Decorate with Tongs" & Bauble Sort**
   - **Concept:** Using plastic toddler training tongs or jumbo tweezers, toddlers pick up soft pom-poms, foam bells, or lightweight shatterproof mini baubles and sort them into matching colored bowls or an empty egg carton "tree".
   - **Why It’s Different:** A focused motor-skills game rather than an art project, encouraging color recognition, pincer grasp, and problem solving.

### Part 3: Scratch Magazine Grinch Nail Art Tutorial

- **Tab:** Tab 103795307
- **Page Title:** Christmas character nail art: how to paint the Grinch - Scratch
- **URL:** https://www.scratchmagazine.co.uk/nail_art/the-grinch-christmas-nail-tutorial/
- **Artist:** UK freehand nail artist Gemma Dawson
- **Design Overview & Step-by-Step Details:**
  - **Base:** Light lime green gel polish base, cured under UV/LED lamp, finished with a non-wipe top coat.
  - **Facial Architecture (Steps 2–9):** Using dark green or black gel paint, paint a central mushroom-shaped nose, a vertical philtrum line, and a lopsided semicircle for the Grinch's signature smirk and pouty lip. Add curved lines for eye sockets and arched, wicked eyebrows.
  - **The "Fur Dragging" Technique (Steps 10 & 13):** While the dark green gel is still wet, use a thicker brush to drag out the perimeter lines into tiny spiky wisps, creating the Grinch's shaggy fur texture around the head, chin, and brows.
  - **Coloring & Shading (Steps 11–16):** Fill the eyes with white gel paint, tint the pouty lip pink, and paint the irises in a bright midtone green. Layer a lighter green gel over the face while dragging edges for depth. Add a green/top-coat wash under the eyes for soft dimensional shadowing.
  - **Fine Detailing (Steps 17–19):** Using a fine liner brush, add pupils, outline the eyes in crisp black, flick thin black hair strokes through the eyebrows to make them bushier, and add pale green highlight streaks along the nose bridge and brow ridge before applying the final top coat.
